title: Chassis and periph MCU images are raw Cortex-M apps linked at 0x08004000 (bootloader not in package)
evidence: Chassis: vector table 0x0-0x12F, SP word0=0x200095F8, Reset word1=0x08004149; Region$$Table at file 0xC54C with literals 0x0801054C/0x0801056C at 0x7B8/0x7BC => base 0x08004000. Periph: SP 0x2000F6F0, Reset 0x08004149, Region$$Table at 0xB120 (load 0x0800F140).
impact: Defines flash map: app at +16 KB, bootloader region 0x08000000-0x08003FFF is flashed separately (not shipped) so app-only updates keep the bootloader.
remediation: Keep bootloader versions documented; include bootloader image in recovery kit.
description: Both images have no ELF/header, begin with the vector table, 60-IRQ table (GD32F30x high-density layout, INFERRED), RW data stored with ARM-Compiler scatter compression (load size 0x29C vs exec 0xA54 chassis; 0x230 vs 0x79C periph). Plaintext, entropy 7.07 and 6.81.

title: Keenon 148-byte IAP tail (length, MD5, version, name) appended to GD32 images
component: chassis tail @0x12E50; periph tail @0xB370; iap_main symbol app_tail (148 B)
evidence: u32 len==tail offset (0x12E50 / 0xB370); MD5 fields 7692ca461c339c7e6fa74113f1e0a202 and 5ad13df946287a8b527104824eb99843 equal recomputed MD5 of payload; version at +20 (v1.1.5-0-g5bec8c6 / v1.1.4-0-g3df9e74); name at +84 ("gd32f3-c40-chassis-app\0bin\0", "gd32f3-c40-periph-app\0bin\0"). iap_main help: file must be app WITHOUT bootloader but WITH tail.
impact: Tail is the only metadata the flasher/bootloader can use for integrity and board-name matching.
remediation: Document the tail format; add an authenticated signature field if tooling is rebuilt.
description: Structure: u32 payload_len, MD5[16], version[64], name+"bin"[64], FF padded. The version/name strings also appear as plain strings inside the payload (0x7514, 0x72D4 chassis).

title: MCU firmware integrity is MD5-only: no signature or authenticity check on GD32 images
evidence: Tail MD5 is recomputed from payload (verified); manifest subPkgMd5 for 06aced7e... and f2bd47fc... equals file MD5; no signature/public-key fields in tail or manifest; no crypto constants (CRC32/MD5/SHA/AES tables) in either image; iap_main contains only mbedtls_md5.
impact: Anyone able to write the package or intercept the transfer can craft a modified image with a valid MD5 tail; MD5 also has known collision weaknesses. Bootloader checks (MSP range, name match) are anti-misflash, not authentication.
remediation: Add asymmetric signature verification in the bootloader (e.g. Ed25519/ECDSA over the payload+version), SHA-256 instead of MD5, and anti-rollback counter.
description: Absence of verification inside the (unavailable) bootloader cannot be proven; however all evidence available (tail layout, host tool) shows MD5 as the only check.

title: MCU images are plaintext (no encryption or obfuscation)
evidence: Readable strings and JSON templates (chassis 0x72B4-0x7648, 0xC464; periph 0x2040; ESP images full IDF log strings); vector tables parse cleanly; entropy 6.8-7.15 consistent with code, not ciphertext.
impact: Firmware is trivially reverse-engineerable and clonable; enables targeted attacks on protocol/state machines.
remediation: Consider flash read-out protection (GD32 FMC security protection, ESP flash encryption) if IP protection matters.
description: Not encrypted or compressed apart from ARM scatter-load RW compression.

title: Chassis image embeds an ~26 KB MCS-51 (8051) firmware blob
evidence: mcs51_probe.py: at base 0xC57C 76% of LCALL (0x12) targets land after RET/LJMP vs 35% elsewhere; LJMP vectors at +0/+3/+6 (0x5A4B,0x64CC,0x4B59); byte histogram 0x90/0xE0/0xF0/0xA3; strings BP-M07S001-APP-2420 (0x125E2), BP01 (0x125F6), HuaCLi (0x125FB), BP001 (0x12602). Blob ends at 0x12BB4 = compressed RW load address.
impact: Chassis firmware can carry and probably re-program a secondary 8051-class controller; its update path is unreviewed and unsigned.
remediation: Identify the target MCU (likely battery/BMS, UNKNOWN) and include it in the firmware inventory; disassemble with an 8051 tool.
description: No direct 32-bit pointer to the blob was found (accessed some other way, UNKNOWN). The "BP" prefix meaning is speculative.

title: Periph board runs RT-Thread and drives cleaning actuators over CAN
evidence: tidle @0x72B8; can_recv_sem/can_send_sem @0x2E0C/0x2E1F; i2c_mutex @0x3CC8; water_pump_task_tid @0x35A4; scrb_tid/srb_tid; side_brush(_self_detect) @0x8AA0/0x8AB0; vacuum_motor @0xAD3C; carpet_detection_sensor @0x307C; press_mon @0x5BE8; watch_dog_tid @0xAE78; PendSV 0x0800419A and HardFault 0x0800424C custom handlers.
impact: Defines the scope of the periph controller (brushes, vacuum, pump, sensors) - useful for fault diagnosis and for scoping what an IAP update can break.
remediation: None (informational).
description: RT-Thread inferred from idle-thread name and object naming; peripheral mapping from names (not disassembled). CAN link to chassis is INFERRED.

title: Chassis image: bare-metal control firmware with IMU, magnetic encoders, motor-fault and wheel-lock logic
evidence: IMU nodata/IMU freq @0x1BD7/0x1BE8; magnetic sensor error / encode not cali @0x8E24-0x8E78; Unlocked by key|cmd|bump @0x8EB0-0x8ED0; overcurrent/hardware fault/overheat/body voltage risk/block/Motor overload @0x8EE4-0x8F38; Left/Right @0xC454; system exception stubs at 0x08005BF8-0x08005C00.
impact: Describes the drive-train safety logic; matches Keenon wheel-motor diagnostics.
remediation: None.
description: IRQ set (HD map, INFERRED): DMA0 ch0/2/5/6, ADC0_1, ADC2, CAN0_RX0, TIMER0/1/5/7, USART0-2, UART3-4. RTOS not detected (no thread names).

title: Chassis speaks YD/T 1363.3-style ASCII battery (BMS) frames with valid length and checksum
evidence: LCHKSUM nibbles A (LENID 006) and E (LENID 002) are correct; CHKSUM FC49 and FD29 equal two-complement of the ASCII sum (0x3B7, 0x2D7) - recomputed.
impact: Chassis polls the battery pack using a plain-text, unauthenticated protocol (standard for BMS).
remediation: None; keep link physically protected.
description: Frame structure is confirmed; the attribution to a YD/T 1363.3-family BMS protocol (CID1 0x4A) is INFERRED, MEDIUM.

title: Common device-info JSON schema across chassis, periph and dock firmware
evidence: status/code/msg/data/property/property-name-en/property-name-cn/devices, devices ids 2 and 21, "hw":{"uuid":"%s"}, "FN%d" function nodes.
impact: Host queries a uniform JSON "devices" list; hardware UUID (MCU UID) is exposed to the host.
remediation: Document schema for the diagnostic tooling; treat the UUID as an identifier.
description: The periph entry is appended to the chassis list (trailing %s). sn is empty in one template.

title: base_station-app .bin is an ESP32-S3 ESP-IDF v5.1.2 image (dock controller), not an STM32/GD32 image
evidence: Header e9 05 02 2f entry 0x40375030, chip_id 9 (ESP32-S3); app_desc @0x20 magic 0xABCD5432, project base_station, v1.1.0-0-gf0ff236, 19:19:01 Aug 12 2026, IDF v5.1.2-dirty; XOR checksum 0x2D and appended SHA-256 da7583...5012 verified; strings: valves, pumps, flow meters, charging FSM, error codes 18/26/27/28.
impact: The update script name (update_Stm32.sh) and manifest column work_station_ctl_board_version are misleading; the dock is an ESP32-S3 water/charging station reached via the Schedule gateway.
remediation: Rename scripts/manifest columns; document the real MCU.
description: IDF built from a "dirty" (modified) tree. Dock functions are STRONGLY_SUPPORTED from log strings.

title: Schedule .bin is an ESP32 espnow_doorbell gateway (UART to ESP-NOW call-bell bridge with OTA relay)
evidence: chip_id 0 (ESP32), project espnow_doorbell, v3.1.1, Aug 24 2023 13:39:11, IDF v4.4.2-dirty; commands get version/get channel/get heart/ota start/wifi ota/reboot/toggle forward/clear maclist (0x6D24-0x7000); doorbell_wifi_ota_task; UART_NUM_0; SHA-256 0117...de64 verified.
impact: The device behind /dev/ttyUSBSchedule is the radio gateway; flashing the dock and flashing the gateway both go through it.
remediation: None.
description: Project name "espnow_doorbell" shows the firmware is derived from an ESP-NOW doorbell/example codebase.

title: No secure-boot signature block in either ESP image file
component: base_station-app .bin (ends at 0xBE730 right after SHA-256); Schedule .bin (ends 0xAB600)
evidence: esp_img.py: nothing follows the appended 32-byte SHA-256 in both files; no 0xE7 signature-block sector.
impact: If secure boot is not enabled in eFuses, any image with a valid checksum/SHA-256 boots; the SHA-256 is self-computed and gives no authenticity.
remediation: Enable Secure Boot v2 and flash encryption on production units (note OTA signature flow).
description: Device eFuse state is UNKNOWN (BLOCKED from static analysis); this finding is about the shipped file only.

title: Hard-coded ESP-NOW PMK literal shared by gateway and dock firmware (value redacted)
evidence: identical 22-character literal beginning pmk_door_ followed by a predictable digit sequence; Schedule: esp_now_set_pmk((uint8_t *)CONFIG_ESPNOW_PMK).
impact: Same predictable key in every unit and in two products; anyone with the binary (public download) can derive the PMK. ESP-NOW unicast encryption additionally needs per-peer LMKs (not evidenced).
remediation: Provision per-site/per-unit keys; use per-peer LMK encryption; do not ship keys in firmware.
description: Only the first 16 bytes of a PMK are used by ESP-NOW. Value deliberately not reproduced here.

title: Dock accepts management and OTA frames over ESP-NOW with MAC-based filtering and an open pairing state
evidence: "Allow management cmd(0x%02X) from <MAC>", "Frame MAC mismatch, ignored", "Received MAC pairing command", "Unpair success, back to broadcast mode", "Search response: currently unpaired", "Recv OTA Frame", "OTA SOH: fw_name=%s", "ota_process_eot: size mismatch" (only a size check string; no MD5/signature string found).
impact: If confirmed, a device in radio range could pair with an unpaired dock (or spoof the paired MAC) and push unsigned firmware or valve/pump commands. Raise to High if confirmed.
remediation: Authenticate frames (per-peer LMK or signed commands), require physical pairing confirmation, verify firmware signature before esp_ota_set_boot_partition.
description: Based solely on strings; behaviour of the checks and any encryption flag in esp_now_peer_info were not decoded (Xtensa code not disassembled).

title: Dock UART console accepts unauthenticated actuator and channel commands
evidence: "channel set%hhu", "channel get", "self clean %hhu %hhu", clean_water_valve1/2_open|close, deter_water_pump_open|close, dirty_water_pump_open|close, water_level_print_open|close.
impact: Physical-access attacker can run pumps/valves (flood/dry-run) or change the radio channel.
remediation: Disable or password-protect the console in production builds.
description: No authentication strings were found; verified only by string inventory.

title: Keenon serial framing: AA AA payload+CRC16 (A5-escaped) 55 55, CRC-16 poly 0xA001
component: iap_main generateFrame @0xCA70, crc16_ibm_step @0xC9E1, initTransportCRC @0xD364; ESP strings "UART_TRANS_INIT", "initTransportCRC for uart"
evidence: Hand-decoded Thumb: movs #0xAA twice at start, compares against 0xAA/0x55/0xA5 with 0xA5 prefix writes, two 0x55 trailer bytes, call to crc16_ibm; crc step uses movw 0xA001 and 8 iterations; initTransportCRC stores sendFrame 0xCCB9, generateFrame 0xCA71, receiveByte 0xCDBD. 8192-byte frame buffers.
impact: Common transport lets one tool talk to chassis bootloader, dock and gateway; framing offers integrity only (CRC) with no authentication.
remediation: None.
description: Hand decoding only (no disassembler); escape byte semantics (original byte stored unchanged after 0xA5) taken from the stores seen. Same function names in ESP firmware (CONFIRMED) suggest the same library.

title: iap_main serial IAP protocol: 128-byte packets, SOH header, ACK 0x06/NAK 0x15, bootloader MD5/MSP/name checks
evidence: Strings: "Downloading file size = %d, pack len = %d", SOH:%03d, "Wait SOH ACK timeout", seq/reqseq retransmit messages, MD5 verify fail, MSP-not-in-SRAM, flash MD5 fail, name mismatch, APP successfully boot; hand-decoded cmp #6/#0x15 and range 0x20-0x23; payloads 00 20 21 00 00 00 (reset, 0xD9A8) and 00 62 51 00 01 00 03 (encoder IAP, 0xD9A0).
impact: Describes how GD32 chassis/periph/encoder boards are programmed through the resident bootloader; bootloader checks are MD5, MSP range and board-name only.
remediation: Document protocol; if re-implementing, add signature checks and slot rollback.
description: Message strings (Chinese, translated in the report) describe bootloader errors; the bootloader itself is not in the package (INFERRED behaviour).

title: Release flashing tools ship with symbols; ota_set/serial_cmd also ship full DWARF and developer paths
component: iap_main (256 symtab entries, no DWARF); ota_set_* and serial_cmd_* (.debug_info/.debug_str)
evidence: DWARF comp_dir /home/peanut/ota, /root/cmd, /home/litreily/workspace/esp/esp32_serial_tools/ota (x86 serial.c GCC 7.5.0 Ubuntu 18.04); iap_info_t members status/ack_nack/reqpackseq/packseq/packlen/write_size/fw_size/fd_s/md5/filebuf; global tmparr[2048000].
impact: Leaks internal usernames, build hosts, toolchain and data structures; eases reverse engineering.
remediation: Strip release binaries (strip -s, no -g); build in clean CI.
description: The x86 ota_set links a serial helper from a third-party-looking esp32_serial_tools tree (licence provenance UNKNOWN).

title: Outdated toolchains used for flashing tools (GCC 4.8.4 / Ubuntu 14.04, no PIE)
evidence: ELF EXEC non-PIE at 0x8000; stack-protector present (__stack_chk_fail imported); GNU_STACK RW; iap_main imports sprintf/strncpy; fixed 2048/8192-byte buffers.
impact: Weaker exploit mitigations and unsupported compiler; tools parse serial data from boards (low exposure).
remediation: Rebuild with a supported toolchain, -fPIE -pie, -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE, bounded string functions.
description: Exploitability not assessed (no disassembly).

title: base_station upgrade.sh: chmod -R 777 *, no shebang, no checks
evidence: Content: script_dir=`dirname "$0"`; cd "$script_dir"/..; chmod -R 777 *; bash update_Stm32.sh. No "#!" line.
impact: Makes iap_main, the .bin and scripts world-writable; if the package dir is shared or the script runs as root, a local user can swap the binary/firmware before execution (privilege escalation / malicious firmware). Run-as user is UNKNOWN.
remediation: Use chmod 750 on specific files; add shebang, set -eu, quote paths; extract packages into root-owned dir.
description: The `*` is unquoted and breaks on odd filenames.

title: update_Stm32.sh flashes the first matching .bin with no integrity, version or type check
evidence: `selected_files=($(find . -maxdepth 1 -name "*.bin" | grep -E "$keyword"))`; `"$path/./iap_main" -s -p /dev/ttyUSBSchedule -b 921600 -f "$stm32"`; sudo service keenonrobot stop/start commented out; no md5/sha/sig, no version compare, no status output.
impact: Any file whose name contains base_station is flashed to the dock via the gateway; failure detection depends on iap_main exit code (UNKNOWN); ROS node may still hold the port.
remediation: Verify signature/hash before flashing, compare versions, quote variables, check exit codes, re-enable service stop/start or lock the port.
description: Chinese comments translated in the report. Name "Stm32" is legacy (target is ESP32-S3).

title: Schedule upgrade.sh: fragile control flow and weak success test
evidence: `cd $(dirname $0)/../script` unquoted; unknown arch only echoes; `PACKAGE_NAME=$(basename ../bin/*.bin)`; `sleep 2`; `NEW_V=$(... awk -F- "{print $2}")`; success iff `grep ${NEW_V}` on version string (unanchored substring).
impact: False success if old version equals new or v3.1.1 matches v3.1.10; unknown architecture continues; aarch64 uses 32-bit armhf tools that need multiarch libs; no pre-flash validation.
remediation: Fail fast on unknown arch, anchor the version compare, verify file hash/signature, quote variables, set -euo pipefail.
description: The updateSuccess/updateFail strings are probably parsed by the calling service (other workers).

title: upgradeConfig.json uses MD5 + size only; no signature; https on cloud.robotkeenon.com
evidence: Fields subPkgMd5/subPkgSize/subPkgUrl only; all 10 URLs https://cloud.robotkeenon.com/filesResource/software/<column>/<version>/<file>; isForced=false; seven present files md5/size verified.
impact: Integrity depends on TLS validation in the client and trust in the server; a compromised server/CDN or a TLS-validation bug allows malicious packages with matching MD5. MD5 is collision-prone.
remediation: Add detached signatures (and a signed manifest) verified on the robot; use SHA-256; add min-version/anti-rollback.
description: URLs were not contacted. TLS validation by the client is not assessed here.

title: Misleading naming: stm32_* manifest column and update_Stm32.sh refer to GD32F3 / ESP32-S3 targets
evidence: Chassis column "stm32_main_c40_bottom_ctrl" -> gd32f3-c40-chassis-app; script update_Stm32.sh -> ESP32-S3 dock.
impact: Operators may assume STM32 tooling/bootloaders; legacy naming complicates audits.
remediation: Rename or add mapping documentation.
description: Manifest field typo subPkgVerColumnDetialId is also vendor-defined.

title: ota_set text-command OTA to the ESP32 gateway, optional relay to a call bell by MAC
evidence: Usage "%s <dev> <bin> [-w [mac_addr]]"; strings "ota start", "esp_ota_begin end", "ack_id", "hold on", "wifi ota %s" with sample MAC 98:cd:ac:45:14:04; DWARF globals flag_ota_begin/ack/fail/wait, flag_wifi_ota, tmparr[2048000].
impact: Gateway firmware and bell firmware are updated with an unauthenticated text/serial command channel.
remediation: Authenticate OTA start and verify image signature on the ESP.
description: Baud for ota_set is not a decoded immediate (UNKNOWN; scripts use 921600 for serial_cmd).

title: ota_set has a fixed 2,048,000-byte image buffer
evidence: DWARF .debug_info/.symtab: tmparr size 2048000 in .bss.
impact: Images larger than ~2 MB cannot be sent; current schedule image 701,952 B fits.
remediation: Size-check input and report a clear error; allocate dynamically.
description: Check for explicit bounds checking not done (no disassembly).

title: Schedule firmware shares UART0 between console logs and the robot command protocol
component: Schedule .bin: uart_param_config(UART_NUM_0...) @0x70C8, log strings "Send command: %s" @0x700D and "recv(%d): %s" @0x7035
evidence: Both IDF console (/dev/uart, uart_write) and the app use UART0.
impact: Log noise can corrupt replies of "get version" and OTA acks (script parsing by grep).
remediation: Move logs to another UART or disable log output at runtime during OTA.
description: Inferred from the shared UART number and log strings; not tested.

title: ESP images contain verbose debug logging and panic handlers with ANSI colour logs left in release builds
evidence: Strings: "I (%u) %s: Application information", "ELF file SHA256: ", "Guru Meditation Error: Core", backtrace/register dump labels, "Rebooting...".
impact: Information disclosure over the UART (versions, task names, addresses) and unauthenticated reboot-on-fault behaviour.
remediation: Reduce log level and disable panic dumps in production.
description: Standard ESP-IDF defaults; impact is limited to local serial access.

title: Embedded version strings match the manifest for all four MCU packages
evidence: chassis v1.1.5-0-g5bec8c6 (tail + 0x7514), periph v1.1.4-0-g3df9e74 (tail + 0x202B), dock app_desc v1.1.0-0-gf0ff236, Schedule v3.1.1 (string v3.1.1-0-g11c2ad2 @0x6D30); md5 of chassis/periph equals manifest; zips absent so their md5 not re-verified here.
impact: Release V246 is internally consistent for MCU packages.
remediation: None.
description: zip md5 values (a5fe3462..., 8c939e42...) could not be recomputed because only extracted trees exist.

title: Dock firmware: water system, charging FSM and error codes
evidence: charging_task, CHARGING_FSM (standby/trickle/charging), exceptions codes 26 (battery connector over heat), 27 (charge MOS over heat), 28 (charge voltage over limit), drain pump error 18, self_clean_task, flow_meter_task, detergent ratio 20~40/40~200, ROBOT_DET, machine model.
impact: Gives fault-code meanings for support diagnostics.
remediation: None.
description: Derived from log strings only.

title: No standard crypto/CRC tables in GD32 images; ESP images carry only IDF crypto
component: constant scan of chassis, periph, base_station, Schedule
evidence: No 0x77073096, 0x1021/0xC0C1 tables, MD5 K0 d76aa478, SHA-256 K0 428a2f98 in GD32 images; ESP images: AES S-box (dock 0xBB18) and SHA-256 K (gateway 0x11EB4) from IDF/mbedtls.
impact: Verification is performed elsewhere (bootloader/host) or by computed CRCs; app does not authenticate anything cryptographically.
remediation: None.
description: Absence of constants is not proof of absence of crypto (bitwise implementations).

title: Unauthenticated WebSocket control server bound to all interfaces (TCP 8888)
evidence: WebServerSocket.<init>(int) -> new InetSocketAddress(port) (wildcard); WebServerSocket.PORT=8888; onOpen only tags the connection by the handshake resource descriptor (ALL8888/PC9090/PC9091/PC8888/APP8888) - no token/origin/credential check observed; onMessage -> SocketServerManager.dispatchMessage -> WebServerManager.handleRosInfo (fastjson parse of id/requestType) -> WebSocketHelp.onHandleMessage switch with ~55 requestType values incl. operationAutoCharger, operationNavigationDst/Action, postFactoryReset, operationInstallApp, postWriteInFile, controlCopyFile, postWifiOperation, operationEnvironmentConfiguration, PostDistPath, operationExit.
impact: Any host that can reach the robot Android IP on port 8888 (internal 192.168.64.x, Wi-Fi hotspot "keenon robot", customer LAN) can issue robot-affecting commands (navigate to a target, start/stop charging, factory reset, start app update, change environment, write files). Physical safety relevance because navigation/charging commands reach the robot via PeanutSDK.
remediation: Require authentication on the server (per-session token issued by the on-robot UI), bind to loopback/internal interface only, validate Origin, add authorization per requestType, remove unneeded handlers from production builds.
description: The Android app embeds a java-websocket WebSocketServer for the Vue SPA. The same socket is also used as a proxy for rosbridge (see RIA-003). The server code path has no authentication. Status CONFIRMED for the absence of checks in the inspected methods; actual reachability depends on firewall/network configuration (UNKNOWN).
reproduction: Static only (no execution, no network, no device): open the APK DEX with a DEX parser or JADX and inspect the cited class#method; see installation_assistant_app.md for the traced call chain.

title: Arbitrary file write with path traversal via "postWriteInFile" request
evidence: WebSocketHelp.onHandleMessage maps requestType "postWriteInFile" -> InformationSupport.onWriteFile; onWriteFile: gson2Bean(FileBean) then MapFileUtils.writeFile(HubConstant.SD_BASE_FOLDER + "MapSources", FileBean.fileName, FileBean.jsonData); writeFile: makeRootDirectory, deleteFile, createEmptyFile, new File(dir, name), FileOutputStream.write(String.getBytes()) - no canonicalisation / ".." filtering call is present in the traced bytecode.
impact: Combined with RIA-001: a remote LAN client can create/overwrite files outside the MapSources directory with attacker-chosen content within the app's storage permissions (WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE; if app runs as system/privileged, wider). Possible tampering with maps/configs or planting files consumed by other robot software.
remediation: Reject names containing path separators or "..", resolve and verify canonical path stays under the base directory, restrict to an allow-list of file names, authenticate the caller.
description: writeFile deletes any existing file at the target before writing. Impact depends on privileges of the process (UNKNOWN: whether installed as system app on the robot).
reproduction: Static only (no execution, no network, no device): open the APK DEX with a DEX parser or JADX and inspect the cited class#method; see installation_assistant_app.md for the traced call chain.

title: rosbridge relay: unauthenticated LAN clients can reach ROS (192.168.64.20:9090/9091) through the app
evidence: RosSocketClientManager.ADDRESS="ws://192.168.64.20:" with ports "9090","9091"; send(String) logs "Send 90"/"Send 91"/"Send ALL" and chooses the socket by topic/service name (arrays topic_91/service_91); WebServerSocket.onOpen registers connections as PC9090/PC9091; WebServerManager.handleRosInfo: if requestType empty -> RosSocketClientManager.getINS().send(raw message) else WebSocketHelp.onHandleMessage. SPA connects to ws://<host>:8888?port=PC9090 / PC9091 when not on a phone.
impact: A client on the same network can send rosbridge JSON (publish /cmd_vel, call rosapi/set_param, /reboot, /database/* services, /switch_dest_floor_map, /motor_lock ...) with no authentication, effectively remote control and configuration of the robot ROS graph.
remediation: Do not expose a raw rosbridge relay; whitelist topics/services per authenticated role; restrict to localhost; enable rosbridge authentication on the ROS side.
description: Relay semantics inferred from method strings/calls (message forwarded unmodified when requestType is absent); exact filtering logic of RosSocketClientManager.onMessage/send not fully traced (no register-level analysis).
reproduction: Static only (no execution, no network, no device): open the APK DEX with a DEX parser or JADX and inspect the cited class#method; see installation_assistant_app.md for the traced call chain.

title: Local HTTP server (AndServer, port 8080): unsanitised file download / picture / video endpoints, CORS "*", no real authentication
evidence: ApiControllerAdapter routes GET /file/download, /map/pic, /video/play, /v3/test and POST /login, /file/upload. ApiController.getFile: new File(HubConstant.SD_BASE_FOLDER + "MapSources" + File.separator + fileName) -> FileBody (no traversal check; only File.exists); getPic/playVideo same pattern with DIR_MAP_SOURCES_BIG / DIR_MAP_SOURCES_VIDEO. CorsInterceptor sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and allows GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS. AndService binds to NetUtils.getLocalIPAddress() port 8080.
impact: Read access to arbitrary files readable by the app via "../" in fileName (STRONGLY_SUPPORTED, not exercised); wildcard CORS lets any web page the operator visits call the API from a browser on the same network.
remediation: Canonicalise and confine paths; remove wildcard CORS; require authenticated sessions; drop test endpoints (/v3/test).
description: Server binds to one IP (not 0.0.0.0) as resolved at start; which interface that is (internal 192.168.64.10 vs hotspot) is UNKNOWN statically.
reproduction: Static only (no execution, no network, no device): open the APK DEX with a DEX parser or JADX and inspect the cited class#method; see installation_assistant_app.md for the traced call chain.

title: "login" endpoint performs no credential verification and logs the submitted account and password

title: WsServer websocket control channel and frp reverse tunnel (remote SSH)
evidence: WsServer (ARM32 stripped, websocketpp 0.8.2) strings: actions frpRestart, frpConfig, frpMapConfig, frpDisconnect, frpState, debug_close; builds shell commands "python /usr/bin/update_frpc.py <serverAddr> <serverPort> <remotePort> <token> <taskNo>", "python /usr/bin/update_map_frpc.py", "nginx -s reload", "md5sum %s", writes /etc/nginx/conf.d/mapping.conf and unzips certificate.zip to /etc/ros/runtime/remotemap/. frpc_release_arm: Go 1.16.2, fatedier/frp (client + dashboard assets). frpc_info.ini template: [ssh_robotSn] type=tcp local_ip=127.0.0.1 local_port=22 remote_port=<> with server_addr/server_port/token blank. update_frpc.py starts "./frpc_release_arm -c /etc/ros/runtime/frpc_info.ini" and kills it after 12 h. upstart Websocket_setup.conf: sleep 10; exec /usr/bin/WsServer (log /home/peanut/websocketlog.log). frpc_setup.conf has the frpc start commented out. WsServer listening port is not recoverable by string analysis (UNKNOWN).
impact: A remote party able to send the websocket message can make the robot open an outbound frp tunnel that exposes local sshd (port 22) on a server chosen by the message; message fields are placed into shell command lines (possible command injection if unsanitized - not tested).
remediation: Authenticate the websocket, validate/escape fields, bind to localhost, and pin server addresses.
description: The tunnel exposes SSH only if the attacker also knows or guesses the SSH credentials. The frp server address and token are supplied at runtime, so none are present in this package.

title: OTA update flow lacks integrity/authenticity controls and runs as root
evidence: manifest.json entries contain no hashes/signatures; debs contain only debian-binary, control.tar.gz, data.tar.xz (no signature members); ros_update uses md5 only ("check md5 success/failed", mbedtls_md5) with md5 supplied alongside the URL ("No obj url md5"); installs with `dpkg -i --force-confnew` then `apt-get -y -f install`, executes script/upgrade.sh, stops cron, reboots; manifest places bin/keenon at absolute dest /etc/init.d/ ; maintainer scripts run as root; robot-settings postinst executes `sudo cp` over files in /opt/ros/indigo/lib/python2.7/dist-packages.
impact: An attacker able to supply a package URL+md5 to ros_update (or tamper in transit/at rest) gets root code execution through maintainer scripts/init scripts.
remediation: Sign packages (detached signature verified on device), verify against pinned key, TLS + authentication for the update API.
description: Severity could be Critical if ros_update is proven reachable and unauthenticated; authentication was not analyzed.

title: robotviz login is client-side only with hard-coded key/ciphertext and pre-filled default credentials
status: CONFIRMED (code); whether the constant corresponds to the default credentials NOT_ANALYZED
evidence: Login.js: form state initialised with username "peanut" and a 6-digit numeric default password (starts "12", redacted); onLogin compares AES-ECB encryption of the JSON form object (CryptoJS, key const = 8-char string starting "PE", parsed as hex) to a hard-coded 96-hex-char constant (starts "52"); on match router pushes /home. No server round-trip.
impact: Authentication can be bypassed by anyone with browser dev tools or by connecting to rosbridge directly; the secret material is in the client bundle.
remediation: Do real server-side authentication; remove defaults.
description: The effective key of CryptoJS Hex.parse(<8-char key string>) is only 4 bytes (non-hex characters parse to 0) - INFERRED from library semantics, LOW confidence.

title: CoAP bridge builds sudo shell commands and downloads archives by URL without signature
evidence: Strings: `echo "` / `" | sudo -S sh -c "` / `chmod -R `, /etc/ros/runtime/database/uuidzip/, /tmp/robot/, /work/robot/, QLTftp curl_easy_perform; topic /libcoap/download (url, md5) with md5 only.
impact: Download URLs/paths flow into root shell commands; md5 gives integrity only against corruption.
remediation: Use execve with argument arrays, sign downloads, restrict who can publish /libcoap/download.
description: Password operand source of the `sudo -S` pipe was not recovered.

title: Samba shares exposing /home/peanut and /root/.ros (read-write) and /etc/ros/runtime
status: CONFIRMED (config); INFERRED (copy executes); Samba presence/users UNKNOWN
evidence: smb.conf: [old log path] path=/root/.ros read only=no; [config] path=/etc/ros/runtime read only=yes; [home] path=/home/peanut read only=no; guest ok=no; map to guest = bad user; unix password sync = yes. postinst: `if [ -d "$myPath"]; then cp $SMBCONF_FILE /etc/samba/` - $myPath is undefined and there is no space before `]`; bash evaluates `[ -d "" ]` as the one-argument form `[ -d ]` which is true, so the copy runs if /etc/samba exists (INFERRED, not executed).
impact: If Samba is installed and a weak password exists, remote read/write of home, root-owned log dir and runtime configs is possible.

description: Shares require Samba authentication (guest ok = no).

title: Remote-tools tunnel client and command stack executes strings built from message fields
evidence: update_map_frpc.py: set_file_value(msg) does `eval(data_json)["data"]["config"]` on a JSON string passed on argv (Python 2 eval), and writes arbitrary key/value pairs into /etc/ros/runtime/frpc_info.ini (frp config) which can define arbitrary tunnels (type, local_ip, local_port, remote_port, plugin). update_frpc.py writes server_addr/server_port/remote_port/token from argv into the frp ini.

description: Reachability of the message source depends on ROS-032 exposure.

evidence: fdl-ros lib/fdl/arm32: libfdl.so (contains JSON config text with "host_url":"192.168.64.199:9090"), libdepthsInterface.so, libmapobs.so, libfruit.so, libRobotOperation.a, sensors/depthAB/OpenNI2/Drivers/{liborbbec.so,libOniFile.so,orbbec.ini,libusb-1.0*,libudev*}, sensors/depthBS/{libBerxelUvcDriver.so,params100Q.bin 6,144,000 bytes}; /usr/lib/debug copies with symbols; berxel-camera ships libBerxelHawk and params100Q.bin.

title: Embedded protocol/crypto use: ZeroMQ+libsodium to MX module; md5 only in OTA
evidence: send_depth_node and module_tool: strings tcp://%s:%s, crypto_secretbox / crypto_secretbox_open, username/password length checks (username.length () <= UCHAR_MAX) consistent with a ZeroMQ/libsodium based RPC; ros_update/libcoap use mbedtls_md5 / libkmd5 for integrity.

remediation: Review key management.

title: Exported receiver executes arbitrary shell commands from an unauthenticated broadcast
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml receiver com.keenon.systemservice.SysServiceBroadcastReceiver, no android:exported but has <intent-filter> and targetSdkVersion=22 -> exported by default; no android:permission on the receiver. JADX decompile of SysServiceBroadcastReceiver.onReceive: `if (ServiceDefine.ServiceIntent.ACTION_EXE_CMD.equals(str)) { exeCmd(intent.getStringExtra(KEY_KEENON_DATA)); }`; exeCmd() runs on a pool thread via Lcom/keenon/peanut/core/utils/device/ShellUtil;->exeCmdSync(String) (disassembly: ProcessBuilder{"sh"} / writes the extra text then "exit\n"), result broadcast via com.keenon.action.EXECUTE_CMD_RESULT.
impact: Any app on the device (no permission required) can send this broadcast and have ServiceSystem execute an arbitrary shell command string as the app's process UID, which per sharedUserId=android.uid.system is intended to run as system. This is an arbitrary command execution primitive with no caller authentication.
remediation: Require a signature-level custom permission on the receiver, verify the sending package/UID (getCallingUid via a bound service instead of a broadcast), and remove free-form shell execution from the IPC surface in favor of a fixed set of validated operations.
description: SysServiceBroadcastReceiver is exported by default (targetSdk<31 + intent-filter) and dispatches android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED, com.keenon.action.IMPORT_U_DRIVE_DATA, .SILENT_INSTALL_APP and .EXECUTE_CMD with no permission check. The EXECUTE_CMD branch takes the KEY_KEENON_DATA extra and hands it to a shell.
reproduction: Static: send `am broadcast -a com.keenon.action.EXECUTE_CMD --es keenon_data '<cmd>'` from any installed app (not executed here; reproduction is inferred from code, not observed).

title: Exported receiver copies arbitrary files/directories on request
evidence: JADX: `if (ServiceDefine.ServiceIntent.ACTION_IMPORT_U_DRIVER_FILE.equals(str)) { copyFile(intent.getStringExtra(KEY_FORM_PATH), intent.getStringExtra(KEY_TO_PATH)); }`; copyFile logs 'start copyFile %s to %s' and calls Lcom/keenon/peanut/core/utils/io/FileUtil;->copyFile/copyDirFiles with attacker-supplied source/destination strings (disassembly of FileUtil.copyFile(File,File,int) and copyDirFiles).
impact: Any app can trigger a file/directory copy between two paths of its choosing, limited only by the system-UID process's filesystem permissions; no path validation observed.
remediation: Restrict to a fixed allow-listed source directory (e.g. only the actual U-disk mount) and a fixed destination, verify caller identity, and canonicalize/validate paths against path traversal.
description: Companion branch to SYS-001 in the same unauthenticated receiver.
reproduction: Static: send the IMPORT_U_DRIVE_DATA broadcast with formPath/toPath extras (not executed).

title: Exported receiver triggers the package-install flow for a caller-supplied path
component: ServiceSystem: SysServiceBroadcastReceiver (action com.keenon.action.SILENT_INSTALL_APP) + peanut core AppInstallerUtil
evidence: JADX onReceive: ACTION_SILENT_INSTALL_APP branch reads KEY_FORM_PATH, checks File(path).exists(), then calls Lcom/keenon/peanut/core/utils/android/AppInstallerUtil;->installApp(Context,String) which builds an ACTION_VIEW intent with FileProvider / vnd.android.package-archive and startActivity (disassembly). A separate installAppSilenceVLL overload (`pm install -r `) exists in the same class but is not the one invoked from this receiver (STRONGLY_SUPPORTED, invoke-list shows installApp not installAppSilence called here).
impact: Any app can cause the system to open the package installer UI for an arbitrary local file path; actual install still needs user confirmation via the installer UI (INFERRED, since the invoked overload is the ACTION_VIEW one, not the shell pm install one, for this code path).
remediation: Require a signature permission on the receiver; if silent install is intended, gate installAppSilence behind the same control as SYS-001/002.
description: Third unauthenticated action on the exported receiver.
reproduction: Static only.

title: Unauthenticated exported AIDL services allow arbitrary MQTT publish/subscribe and voice/TTS control
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml: all four services declared android:exported="true" with no android:permission. Bundled .aidl interface files (com/keenon/{voice,tts,aidl/mqtt,bi/aidl}) define execCmd/execCmdAsync, startTts, publish/subscribe/observer with caller-chosen String topic and String appFlag, and IBiManager.send(event, properties, ap, versionName). MqttAidlApiImpl.publish/subscribe forward directly to Lcom/keenon/component/core/mqtt/MqttApiProxy;->publish/subscribe without a topic allow-list (dexscan invoke list for MqttAidlApiImpl).
impact: Any app that knows the AIDL interfaces (shipped inside the APK, trivially extractable) can bind these services without any permission and publish to, or receive from, arbitrary MQTT topics under the device's cloud identity, inject BI events, and drive TTS/voice behavior.
remediation: Add a signature-level permission to each <service>, validate caller UID/package against an allow-list (peanut-clean, robot-installation-assistant, launcher), and restrict the MQTT topic namespace reachable from AIDL callers.
description: The four system services that back the vendor serviceSdk client libraries are reachable by any app on the device.
reproduction: Static only; AIDL stubs are present in both ServiceSystem and in peanut-clean/robot-installation-assistant (classes.json cls listing).

title: MQTT-delivered remote shell command execution
evidence: Disassembly of SshMqttProxy$2.onMessageArrived: payload on SshConstants.getCmdTopic() ("/android/remote/cmd/frp_%s") is turned into a String and passed to APPCmdHelper.ins().inputCmd(json). Disassembly/JADX of APPCmdHelper.inputCmd: `JSONObject(str).getString("msg")` then `ShellUtil.exeCmd(msg, callback)`; the callback (APPCmdHelper$1) logs and calls onResponseData, which publishes {isSuccess,data} back on the cmd_resp topic via SshMqttProxy.publish.
impact: Whoever can publish to the per-serial-number MQTT command topic (the vendor cloud broker, or anyone who can reach/spoof it) can execute an arbitrary shell command on the tablet as the RemoteControl process (sharedUserId android.uid.system).
remediation: Authenticate and authorize the MQTT connection end-to-end (mutual TLS/ACLs restricting publish to the device's own topic), sign/validate command payloads, and avoid free-form shell execution.
description: This is a legitimate maintenance feature by design (remote shell for support), but its security rests entirely on the MQTT broker's access control, which is outside this APK and was not analyzed.
reproduction: Static only; requires MQTT broker access, not available/attempted in this environment.

title: adb over TCP enabled unconditionally at init and reachable through the FRP tunnel
evidence: JADX decompile of SystemInitializer.init: `ShellUtil.exeCmd("setprop service.adb.tcp.port 5678\nstop adbd\nstart adbd", null);` runs unconditionally (not gated by build flavor) after the fusion-board branch. FrpClientHelper.buildFrpClientConfig/buildMapFrpClientConfig strings include `local_port = 5678` (DEX string table, FrpClientHelper ms output).
impact: adbd is switched to listen on TCP port 5678 at every ServiceSystem init, and the vendor FRP tunnel forwards that same local port to a remote server when triggered by MQTT (SYS-005's channel). If adb is unauthenticated (ro.adb.secure=0) or the key is pre-authorized, this exposes a full adb shell to whoever controls the FRP/cloud path.
remediation: Do not expose adb over TCP in production; if needed for support, gate it behind a short-lived, explicitly user-approved flow, and never bridge it through an externally reachable tunnel.
description: The same constant (5678) appears both as the adb TCP port set at boot and as the frpc local_port, which combined with the exported FRP flow is a built-in remote-adb layer.
reproduction: Static correlation of two constants; not dynamically verified.

title: Hard-coded SMB root credentials for the robot-side host
evidence: Disassembly of SMBManager.lambda$init$0$SMBManager: `new AuthenticationContext("root", SMBInterface.PASS_LIST[passIndex].toCharArray(), "DOMAIN")` then `SMBClient().connect("192.168.64.20")`.authenticate(...). SMBInterface.<clinit> builds a 2-entry String[] PASS_LIST with filled-new-array of two short string constants (values not reproduced here; type=hard-coded password, length redacted).
impact: A fixed, reverse-engineerable root password set for the SMB server at 192.168.64.20 (the ROS/robot side host) is embedded in the APK; anyone who extracts the APK gets root SMB credentials to the robot compute unit.
remediation: Do not hard-code root credentials; use per-device provisioned, rotated credentials or certificate-based auth; least-privilege SMB account instead of root.
description: Static string/byte-code constant; exact values intentionally not printed (REDACT: 2 string constants, class com.keenon.peanut.uploadlog.smb.SMBInterface, field PASS_LIST).
reproduction: Static only.

title: Hard-coded third-party LLM API bearer keys in code
evidence: dexscan string extraction, KimiChatApi#initUrlConnectionAuthVL: Authorization header literal "Bearer sk-<REDACTED 51 chars>" alongside getLLMChatApiUrl()=https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/chat/completions; DeepseekChatApi#initUrlConnectionAuthVL: "Bearer sk-<REDACTED 32 hex chars>" alongside getLLMChatApiUrl()=https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions (model string "deepseek-v3").

remediation: Move LLM keys server-side; the app should call a Keenon-operated proxy that holds the real provider keys, not embed them.
description: REDACT: type=API key (Bearer token), location=Lcom/keenon/systemservice/voice/ctrl/nlp/kimi/KimiChatApi;->initUrlConnectionAuthVL and .../deepseek/DeepseekChatApi;->initUrlConnectionAuthVL. Values not reproduced.
reproduction: Static only.

title: Hard-coded Azure OpenAI / Speech keys for 8 regions in a bundled asset
evidence: JSON asset contains 8 entries (Japan East Free, Japan East, US East, Europe West, Australia East, Brazil South, South Africa North, UAE North), each with openaiKey, speechKey (both 84-character base64-like secrets) plus openaiDomain/speechDomain host names (*.openai.azure.com, *.api.cognitive.microsoft.com).
impact: Eight Azure OpenAI and Azure Cognitive Speech subscription keys are shipped in plaintext inside the APK assets, directly usable by anyone who extracts the file; significant abuse/cost risk and possible resource exhaustion against the vendor's Azure subscriptions.
remediation: Do not ship cloud provider keys in the client; proxy requests through a Keenon-controlled backend that holds the keys server-side and authenticates the device.
description: REDACT: type=cloud API keys (8x openaiKey, 8x speechKey), location=assets/voiceConfig/micro_resource.json inside the ServiceSystem APK. Values not reproduced.
reproduction: Static only; file is plain JSON, directly readable after unzip.

title: iFlytek robot-platform credentials and an RSA private key shipped in assets
evidence: robot.json / robot_test.json contain appId and secret fields for the iFlytek robot gateway (service.iflybot.com.cn, ws://robot.iflybot.com.cn/robot/engine/v2_2); assets/vtn/privateKey.pem is a PEM block beginning '-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----' (1700 bytes) alongside a matching publicKey.pem, referenced from assets/vtn/vtn.ini.
impact: A vendor-issued appId/secret pair and a private RSA key are embedded in the package; if used for authenticating to the iFlytek service or local VTN voice engine, their disclosure could allow quota abuse or impersonation.
remediation: Rotate these credentials if they are production-shipping secrets; avoid storing private keys in app assets; use per-device provisioning instead.
description: REDACT: type=appId/secret pair (robot.json, robot_test.json) and RSA private key (assets/vtn/privateKey.pem). Values not reproduced.
reproduction: Static only.

title: Process-wide trust-all TLS and hostname verifier
evidence: Disassembly: AllowX509TrustManager.checkClientTrusted/checkServerTrusted bodies are `return-void` (no checks); AllowX509TrustManager$1.verify(String,SSLSession) returns `const/4 v1,#1; return v1` (always true); allowAllSSL() calls HttpsURLConnection.setDefaultHostnameVerifier(this) and setDefaultSSLSocketFactory(ctx.getSocketFactory()), i.e. it replaces the JVM-wide defaults.
impact: Once SecurityKeyManager.init runs, every HttpsURLConnection in the process (not just the intended call) accepts any TLS certificate for any hostname, enabling trivial man-in-the-middle interception/tampering of HTTPS traffic from this app.
remediation: Never install a trust-all manager/hostname verifier; use proper certificate pinning or the platform default trust store for the control-plane traffic that needs it.
description: Global, not scoped to one connection.
reproduction: Static only.

title: MQTT TLS trust check is a substring match on certificate subject, not real validation
evidence: Disassembly of DynamicMqttServer$2.checkTrusted(X509Certificate[]): for each cert, `getSubjectDN().toString()` is checked with `String.contains("keenon.com")`; if any certificate in the chain lacks that substring, a CertificateException is thrown, otherwise the chain is accepted - there is no chain-of-trust, expiry or hostname validation. ClientSSLSocketFactory$1 (RemoteControl) performs the identical pattern for its MQTT TLS connection.
impact: An attacker who can present any certificate whose Subject DN happens to contain the literal string "keenon.com" (e.g. a self-signed cert with CN=notkeenon.com.attacker.example or any field containing that substring) will be trusted by the MQTT TLS layer, defeating certificate validation for the MQTT broker connection used for remote commands, telemetry and log notification topics.
remediation: Use standard X509 chain validation against a pinned CA, and match the full expected hostname/CN exactly rather than a substring.
description: Both apps implement the same flawed pattern, likely shared code lineage.
reproduction: Static only.

title: Cleartext transports and cleartext permitted at the application level
component: ServiceSystem and RemoteControl manifests (android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"); multiple http:// and tcp:// (non-TLS MQTT) endpoints
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml <application usesCleartextTraffic="true"> on both ServiceSystem and RemoteControl. String evidence: http://console.peanut.keenonrobot.com:80, http://corrector.keenonrobot.com:80, http://robotnlp.keenonrobot.com:80, http://iss.openspeech.cn/v, tcp://console.peanut.keenonrobot.com (SshMqttServer, RemotePeanutServer default URLs), Sentry DSN meta-data uses http:// scheme.
impact: Several control-plane and telemetry channels run over plaintext HTTP/TCP, exposing data (and in the MQTT/EXECUTE_CMD cases, command traffic) to network-level interception or tampering when the device is on an untrusted network.
remediation: Move all traffic to TLS with certificate pinning; remove usesCleartextTraffic=true and add a proper network_security_config enforced from the manifest (the existing one in ServiceSystem is not referenced - see SYS-014-adjacent gap note).
description: Cross-cutting network hygiene finding.
reproduction: Static only.

title: Generic/shared platform signing identity across system-privileged apps
evidence: certinfo.py: all three APKs (plus peanut-clean) share one v1 certificate, subject/issuer 'C=US, ST=California, L=Mountain View, O=Android, OU=Android, CN=Android, E=android@android.com', serial 00ff0641323cf95512, SHA-256 2d370c21f5dfd553d2a796314b70925fb38adeef90864c920bbbbb12887d3522, validity 2014-12-23..2042-05-10. robot-installation-assistant uses a different cert (CN=keenon).
impact: Because sharedUserId=android.uid.system requires a matching platform signature, any party possessing this well-known-pattern 'Android' test/AOSP-style key (common on many AOSP-derived platform builds) could in principle sign and install a package sharing the same UID and permissions as these apps on a device using this same platform key. Whether this specific private key is restricted to the vendor's build pipeline is UNKNOWN (could not be assessed statically); using a generic AOSP-style subject name for a platform key is itself a code-smell suggesting it may originate from a shared/public Rockchip SDK signing key rather than a vendor-unique one.
remediation: Confirm the platform signing key is unique and tightly controlled by the OEM/vendor build process; if it is a widely distributed Rockchip SDK test key, replace it with a vendor-unique platform key.
description: Evidence is limited to certificate metadata; private key custody could not be assessed.
reproduction: Static certificate comparison.

title: krlog's sharedUserId is declared on <application>, not <manifest>
evidence: Decoded manifest: `<application android:... android:sharedUserId="android.uid.system" ...>` - the attribute appears on the <application> element; the <manifest> root element has no sharedUserId attribute in the same decode.
impact: The Android platform parses sharedUserId only from <manifest>; if this is indeed how the binary XML is structured (not a decoder artifact), krlog would install with its own UID, not the shared system UID, meaning its READ_LOGS/INSTALL_PACKAGES/DELETE_PACKAGES/READ_PRIVILEGED_PHONE_STATE permission requests would only succeed if independently granted as privileged/signature permissions by the platform. This could be either a packaging defect (unintentionally weaker app) or the decoder's attribute-sorting may simply place it under the nearest preceding start-tag in this minimal parser - verification against the installed device's process UID is needed.
remediation: Verify sharedUserId placement with a canonical AAPT/apktool decode and, on a test device, check the running UID of com.keenon.krlog; correct the manifest if the placement is wrong.
description: Flagged as a possible manifest authoring defect; confidence is MEDIUM because it rests on one custom AXML decoder's output.
reproduction: Re-decode AndroidManifest.xml with a second independent tool (apktool/aapt2) to confirm; not done in this engagement (no apktool permitted).

title: androidx.test instrumentation activities exported in a release build
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml: all three declared with android:exported="true" and an action.MAIN intent-filter, inside the production RemoteControl manifest (not a separate androidTest APK).
impact: Test-support activities intended for instrumentation test harnesses are present and launchable in the shipped release APK; while individually low-capability, this increases attack surface and indicates androidx.test dependencies were not stripped from the release build.
remediation: Exclude androidx.test from the release build variant / use testImplementation scope only, or explicitly set exported=false for these activities in the release manifest.
description: Matches the scope item about androidx.test InstrumentationActivityInvoker exported activities in release builds.
reproduction: Static manifest inspection.

title: Hard-coded AES/keystore material and a native key map, secrets cached in unencrypted MMKV/SharedPreferences
component: ServiceSystem/RemoteControl: lib*/libcipher_pack.so (CipherUtil.get); RemoteControl: com.keenon.common.mqtt.ClientSSLSocketFactory.create (eng flavor), com.keenon.peanut.core.security.AesUtil.generateKeyOrIV, com.keenon.common.http.manager.ConfigManager (defaultMMKV getters for mqtt user/password, security AES key/IV, RSA keys)
evidence: soinv.py: libcipher_pack.so exports data symbols BUGLY_APPID_ENG/PROD, BUGLY_APPKEY_ENG/PROD, UMENG_APPKEY and contains short plaintext string constants alongside keys such as aes_dev_key, aes_dev_iv, ssl_key_pwd_test/prod, ssl_trust_pwd_test/prod, md5_secret_key, amap_appkey, peanut_mqtt_u/p[_prod], selected via getPkgNameByContext/matchCipherStrFromMap per caller package. ClientSSLSocketFactory.create (disassembly) has two literal String constants (lengths 8 and 16; values redacted) used as keystore passwords for the eng-flavor BKS keystores. AesUtil.generateKeyOrIV uses a fixed 62-character alphabet string as its character pool (not itself a secret, but the keygen approach is visible). ConfigManager getters (getMqttUserName/Password, getSecurityAesKey/Iv, getSecurityRsaPrivate/PublicKey) read from MMKV.defaultMMKV(), which is not configured with encryption in the traced call (MMKV supports AES-encrypted stores but no encryption key argument was observed at the call sites examined).
impact: A static, extractable key/credential map keyed only by caller package name provides limited protection (obfuscation, not a secret boundary); eng-flavor MQTT TLS keystore passwords are plaintext constants; and runtime-resolved secrets (MQTT password, AES key/IV, RSA keys) are cached in an MMKV store that, as called, does not appear to use MMKV's own encryption option, making them readable by anything with root/backup access to app data.
remediation: Use Android Keystore-backed secrets instead of a static native lookup table; never ship symmetric keystore passwords in code; enable MMKV encryption (or use EncryptedSharedPreferences) for any cached secret.
description: REDACT: type=multiple hard-coded key labels/short secrets inside libcipher_pack.so and ClientSSLSocketFactory.create. Values not reproduced beyond already-public-looking labels (BUGLY/UMENG are commonly public SDK app IDs, not necessarily sensitive by themselves).
reproduction: Static only (ELF export table + string scan + disassembly).

title: allowBackup=true on all three system apps
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml <application android:allowBackup="true"> in ServiceSystem, RemoteControl and krlog; no android:fullBackupContent restriction observed.
impact: If adb backup / auto backup is reachable (requires USB debugging or an account-backed backup; mitigated if adb is secured), app data including cached secrets (MMKV/SharedPreferences, see SYS-017) and logs could be extracted.
remediation: Set allowBackup=false for privileged system components, or scope backups to exclude secret-bearing files.
description: Low severity on its own; compounds SYS-006 (adb exposure) and SYS-017 (cached secrets).
reproduction: Static only.

title: Secrets written to logcat, which krlog then stores persistently on shared storage
component: ServiceSystem: com.keenon.component.core.mqtt.DynamicMqttServer.getKeyPwd/getTrustPwd (debug logging); krlog: com.keenon.krlog.utils.LogcatHelper (captures `logcat` to files)
evidence: Disassembly of DynamicMqttServer.getKeyPwd(String): after resolving the password via CipherUtil.get, it calls KLogProxy$ModuleLogger.d(tag, "getKeyPwd %s => %s", [param, resolvedValue]) - the resolved password value is passed as a format argument to a debug log call. krlog's LogcatHelper$LogDumper runs `logcat` and writes every line verbatim to /sdcard/krlog/... files (section 4.3).
impact: If this debug log level is active, resolved keystore passwords are written to the system log, and krlog's full-device logcat capture would persist them in plaintext files on external storage, which can then be exported via USB (krlog UI) or uploaded by RemoteControl's log-upload feature.
remediation: Never log secret values, even at debug level; add log scrubbing for known sensitive keys before any log is persisted or uploaded.
description: Chain of two otherwise-separate apps' behavior combining into a disclosure path.
reproduction: Static only; log level gating (whether debug logs are compiled/enabled in production) not verified.

title: Remote desktop with input injection launched from a world-writable-adjacent temp path
evidence: JADX decompile: `ClientSdkManager.LaunchExternalProcess(this.mSandboxPath, LOCAL_TEMP_PATH, "liborayinput_agent5.so", " -o 0", false)` and similar, with LOCAL_TEMP_PATH referencing /data/local/tmp/ (string evidence: '/data/local/tmp/'). INJECT_EVENTS permission is requested in the manifest.
impact: Native remote-control helper binaries are copied to and executed from /data/local/tmp; if that directory or the copy step is not tightly permissioned, a local attacker (e.g. another app with shell access) could race or substitute the binary. The remote desktop feature itself grants a cloud-authenticated operator full screen view and input injection on the tablet.
remediation: Execute helper binaries from the app's private directory (filesDir) rather than /data/local/tmp, verify binary integrity (signature/hash) before exec, and ensure INJECT_EVENTS usage is gated by the same authentication as session creation.
description: Design-level: remote-control/input-injection functionality is powerful by nature; the main static concern is the use of a shared temp path.
reproduction: Static only.

title: Cloud-controlled nginx/map config deployment with native shell helper and no observed filename validation
evidence: JADX decompile of handleNginxFile: file/fileName and certificate.file/certificate.fileName come directly from the parsed MQTT JSON payload (FrpNginxMapConfigBean.NginxConfig) and are concatenated into shell-style commands run through KNNativeTool.nativeCmd: `/system/bin/cp <BASE_PATH><certFileName> <MAP_NGINX_PEM_DIR>/<certFileName>`, `/system/bin/unzip /oem/etc/ros/runtime/remotemap/<certFileName> -d <MAP_NGINX_PEM_DIR>/`, `/system/bin/cp <BASE_PATH><fileName> <MAP_NGINX_CONFIG_DIR>/<fileName>`, finishing with `/system/bin/ubuntu1604 xargs nginx -s reload`; libnativetool.so (ELF import list) imports socket/sendto/recvfrom and exposes one JNI export nativeCmd, consistent with a local command-proxy socket rather than a direct shell exec (dexscan/elfinfo evidence); the exact transport/validation inside the native proxy was not decompiled.
impact: Filenames taken from a cloud-delivered MQTT message are embedded into constructed command strings for cp/unzip/nginx reload; if the native proxy does not itself sanitize them, this is a path-traversal / command-injection surface reachable by whoever can publish to the FRP MQTT command channel (same trust boundary as SYS-005).
remediation: Validate/escape all filenames from untrusted payloads before use in any command string, and prefer parameterized file operations (Java File APIs) over shelling out to cp/unzip.
description: The actual sanitization, if any, happens inside the native nativeCmd proxy, which was not reverse engineered beyond its import table; severity/likelihood could not be fully confirmed.
reproduction: Static only; native proxy behavior NOT_ANALYZED.

title: Exported voice deep-link activities and boot receivers (lower-severity exported surface)
component: ServiceSystem: voice.config.VoiceConfigActivity, voice.config.VoiceActivationActivity (scheme keenon://solution.scene.voice/*); RemoteControl: daemon.RobotBootReceiver, HeadService, CommonService; krlog: AutoStartBroadcastReceiver, LogService
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml: VoiceConfigActivity/VoiceActivationActivity exported=true with VIEW/BROWSABLE intent-filters on the keenon:// scheme; RobotBootReceiver/HeadService exported by default (BOOT_COMPLETED filter / explicit exported=true); krlog LogService exported=true, AutoStartBroadcastReceiver exported by default (BOOT_COMPLETED filter).
impact: These components accept external Intents/links with limited but non-zero effect (open config UI, start/stop log capture, keep-alive). Individually low risk; included for completeness of the exported-component inventory.
remediation: Review whether each truly needs to be exported; set exported=false where only internal use is intended.
description: General exported-surface hygiene item distinct from the high-severity command/file findings above.
reproduction: Static manifest inspection.

title: Full device logcat persisted to shared external storage with no file-level access control
evidence: Disassembly/JADX: LogcatHelper$LogDumper captures all of `logcat` (not app-scoped) into /sdcard/krlog/... text files, rotated/zipped; MainActivity exports these to a USB stick found by scanning /storage/*.
impact: Any app with READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (broadly granted pre-scoped-storage on targetSdk 22) can read the same log files that may contain other apps' sensitive log lines (see SYS-019), and a user with physical USB access can export the full log history.
remediation: Store logs in app-private storage, or restrict to a dedicated, access-controlled partition; scrub known-sensitive content before export.
description: Consequence of krlog's design rather than a coding bug.
reproduction: Static only.

title: LLM system prompt can be overridden from a file on writable external storage
evidence: DEX string: "/sdcard/peanut/voice/gptSystemDesc.txt" found alongside the default system-role text class (init body constant) in the LLM nlp package (dexscan string table, voice/ctrl/nlp/llm constructor).
impact: If this path is read at runtime to override the LLM system prompt (not fully traced), any app or user with storage write access could change the robot assistant's persona/instructions, which is a low-severity but notable integrity issue for an AI assistant feature.
remediation: If the override capability is intentional for field customization, move it to protected app storage or validate/sign its contents; otherwise remove external-storage sourcing for prompt content.
description: The read path into this constant was not traced to a specific method in this engagement; included as INFERRED LOW-severity finding based on a strong string co-location signal.
reproduction: Static string evidence only.
